links.comparator_used: Pre-implementation period under standard care (clinical reminders and USPSTF eligibility criteria), in an interrupted time series
links.outcome: Lung cancer screening uptake, and benefit-based uptake (high-benefit vs intermediate-benefit persons)
links.effect: Benefit-based LCS OR 1.03 (0.82-1.31) pre-implementation, 1.81 (1.34-2.46) during implementation, 1.55 (1.41-1.72) post-implementation. By the final month, predicted screening probability was 24.8% for high-benefit vs 15.8% for intermediate-benefit persons (mean absolute difference 9.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.6%-16.5%). Overall uptake rose 6% per month. This is an uncontrolled before-after design and other site initiatives may have contributed to the overall rise.
links.quote: The association between predicted benefit on LCS uptake was greater after tool implementation; that is, more benefit-based LCS.

design_hint: prediction-augmented shared decision-making decision support tool with benefit-tailored screening encouragement
